docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < seq_n i) →
      StrictMono seq_n → ∃ d, {x | ∀ (i : ℕ), ↑x < ↑(seq_n i) ∨ ¬↑x ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD ↑(seq_n i)]}.HasLogDensity d

docstring: Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varespilon}(N^\varespilon)
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, (fun N => ↑(Erdos30.h N) - √↑N) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ ε

docstring:
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : Finset ℤ), max ↑(A + A).card ↑(A * A).card ≥ C * ↑A.card ^ (2 - ε)

docstring:
The Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture states that there is a constant $c(H) > 0$ for each
$H$ such that we can take $f(n) = n^{c(H)}$ in the above formulation.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
    ∃ c > 0, Erdos61.IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H fun n => ↑n ^ c

docstring:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.
references: [Er87b] Erdős, P., Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[Ko24c] Z. Kovács, A note on Erdős's mysterious remark. arXiv:2412.05190 (2024).
type_pretty: (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ¬Erdos91.UniqueMinimizer n) ↔ True

docstring:
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?
references: [[Er75f](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=411984)] Erdős, Paul, On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
[[Er83c](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=706025)] Erdős, Paul, Combinatorial problems in geometry. Math. Chronicle (1983), 35-54.
[[Er87b](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=910710)] Erdős, P., Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[[Er90](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1117038)] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990), 467-478.
[[Er92b](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1275857)] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics. Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.
[[EFPR93](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1210096)] Erdős, Paul and Füredi, Zoltán and Pach, János and Ruzsa, Imre Z., The grid revisited. Discrete Math. (1993), 189-196.
[[Er94b](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1304854)] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
[[Er97e](https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=1487304)] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos98.h n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

docstring:
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
references: [BEGL96] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Li, W. Wen-Ching, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers. Acta Arith. (1996), 133-138.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ),
    k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (D : Finset ℕ),
        (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) →
          1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (↑d - 1)⁻¹ →
            D.gcd id = 1 → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, Erdos124.sumsOfDistinctPowers d k

docstring:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$
references: [Be68] Berlekamp, E. R., A construction for partitions which avoid long arithmetic progressions. Canad. Math. Bull. (1968), 409-414.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[Go01] Gowers, W. T., A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem. Geom. Funct. Anal. (2001), 465-588.
type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(Erdos138.W k) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

docstring: Is the limit $F(N)/N$ as $N \to \infty$ irrational?
type_pretty: True ↔ Irrational (Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑(Erdos168.F N) / ↑N) Filter.atTop)

docstring:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ f, Continuous f ∧ ∀ (c : NNReal), {n | ↑(primeGap n) / Real.log ↑n < ↑c}.HasDensity (f c)

docstring:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

docstring: Is it true that $$N(b) \ll \log \log b$$?
type_pretty: True ↔ (fun b => ↑(Erdos304.smallestCollectionTo b)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun b => Real.log (Real.log ↑b)

docstring:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

Asked by Barbeau [Ba76].

[Ba76] Barbeau, E. J., _Computer challenge corner: Problem 477: A brute force program._
type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ P Q, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

docstring:
Is it true that for sufficiently large $n$, for any $\delta_k\in \{-1,0,1\}$,
$$\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{\delta_k}{k}\right\rvert > \frac{1}{[1,\ldots,n]}$$
whenever the left-hand side is not zero?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (δ : Fin n → ℚ),
      δ '' Set.univ ⊆ {-1, 0, 1} → |∑ k, δ k / (↑↑k + 1)| ≠ 0 → |∑ k, δ k / (↑↑k + 1)| > 1 / ↑((Finset.Icc 1 n).lcm id)

docstring: Can one show that $\sum_{n\leq x}g_k(n) \sim c_k x\log x$ for some constant $c_k$?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ c,
      Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, ↑(Erdos400.g k n)) fun x =>
        c * ↑x * Real.log ↑x

docstring:
Let $σ_1(n) = σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.

Is it true that $\lim_{k → ∞} σ_k(n)^{\frac 1 k} = ∞$?

This is problem (iii) from
Erdos, Granville, Pomerance, Spiro
"On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetical functions"
(page 169 of the book "Analytic Number Theory", 1990).
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ n > 1, Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑((⇑(ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1))^[k] n) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

docstring: Are there infinitely many barriers for `ω`?
type_pretty: True ↔ {n | Erdos413.IsBarrier (fun m => ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m)) n}.Infinite

docstring:
Let $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Is it true that$$\liminf_{n\to \infty} n \| n\alpha \|
\| n\beta\| =0$$? This is also known as the Littlewood conjecture.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (α β : ℝ), Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑n * distToNearestInt (↑n * α) * distToNearestInt (↑n * β)) Filter.atTop = 0

docstring:
Let $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$. Let $B ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ be the set of integers which are representable
in exactly one way as the sum of two elements from $A$. Is it true that for all
$\epsilon > 0$ and large $N$, $|\{1,\ldots,N\} \setminus B| \gg_\epsilon N^{1/2 - \epsilon}$?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), ∀ ε > 0, Erdos14.almostSquareRoot ε =O[Filter.atTop] Erdos14.nonUniqueSumCount A

docstring:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the number of divisors of $n$. Is there some $n > 24$ such that
$$
  \max_{m < n}(m + \tau(m)) \leq n + 2?
$$
type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ n > 24, ⨆ m, ↑m + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m ≤ n + 2

docstring:
**Erdős problem 681.**
Is it true that for all large $n$ there exists $k$
such that $n + k$ is composite and $p(n+k) > k^2$,
where $p(m)$ is the least prime factor of $m$ ?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k > 0, (n + k).Composite ∧ ∀ (p : ℕ), Erdos681.IsLPF p (n + k) → p > k ^ 2

docstring:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$
such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$
and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ A, 1 - ε ≤ (A + A).lowerDensity ∧ (Nat.cast ∘ AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => 1

docstring: Variant using the exact simultaneous double product property from [CKS05, 4.1].
references: [CKS05] Cohn, H., Kleinberg, R., Szegedy, B., and Umans, C. "Group-theoretic Algorithms for Matrix Multiplication" (Problem 4.7)
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ ε > 0,
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ H x,
        ∃ (_ : Finite H),
          ∃ A B,
            ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(Nat.card H) ∧
              ↑(Nat.card H) ≤ ↑n ^ (2 + ε) ∧
                (∀ (i : Fin n), ↑n ^ (2 - ε) ≤ ↑(A i).card * ↑(B i).card) ∧ Green36.SimultaneousDoubleProduct A B

docstring:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Is it true that, for all large $n$, the number of divisors of $n$ in
$(n^{1/2},n^{1/2}+n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ is $O_\epsilon(1)$?

Erdős attributes this conjecture to Ruzsa.
references: [ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ K, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (Erdos886.Erdos886Divisors n ε 1).card ≤ K

docstring:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r > 0,
    ∃ k,
      ∀ (I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ),
        (∀ (i : Fin r), 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin r), i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ i, ∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)

docstring:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?
references: [Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) / (↑↑n * ↑(Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = ⊤

docstring:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ r ≥ 1, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k r

docstring:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a set containing no solutions to $a + b = c$.
Must there be a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R} \setminus S$ of cardinality continuum such that
$A + A \subseteq \mathbb{R}\setminus S$?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (S : Set ℝ), (∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∉ S) → ∃ A ⊆ Sᶜ, Cardinal.mk ↑A = Cardinal.continuum ∧ A + A ⊆ Sᶜ

docstring:
Main conjecture:

$\log k(n) \le (\log n)^{(1/2 + o(1))}$
references: [Er65] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in number theory. Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. VIII (1965), 181-189.
[Er76e] Erdős, P., Problems and results on consecutive integers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1976), 271-282.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ ε,
    (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.log ↑(Erdos962.k n) ≤ (Real.log ↑n).rpow (1 / 2 + ε n)

docstring: Is it true that if $m < k$ then $f_{k,m}(x) \gg x^{m/k}$ for sufficiently large $x$?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (k m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m < k → (fun x => ↑x ^ (↑m / ↑k)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Erdos323.f k m x)

docstring:
Let $k ≥ 2$, and let $f_k(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n = p_1^k + \dots + p_k^k$,
where the $p_i$ are prime numbers. Is it true that $\limsup f_k(n) = \infty$?
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2, Filter.limsup (fun n => (Erdos979.solutionSet n k).encard) Filter.atTop = ⊤

docstring:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ p, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), ∃ boundaries, ∃ (_ : StrictMono boundaries), Erdos1056.AllModProdEqualsOne p boundaries

docstring:
Erdős asked whether the limiting density `f n / n` exists and, if so, whether it is
irrational.
type_pretty: (∃ l, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos1062.f n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds l) ∧ Irrational l) ↔ True

docstring:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear ↑A → A.card / 2 ≤ EuclideanGeometry.distinctDistances A

docstring:
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
references: [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
[Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe, Warsaw (1960).
[FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers, Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.
type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), k.IsSierpinskiNumber → k.IsPerfectPower ∨ Erdos1113.HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k

docstring:
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal. Must there exist a cardinal $\lambda$ such that every
graph with chromatic number $\lambda$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number
$\kappa$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent when
$\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ (see `erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`).
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (κ : Cardinal.{u_1}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          G.chromaticCardinal = μ → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

docstring:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.
references: [ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑{n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.card / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

docstring:
Can $25$ be written as
$$25=\frac{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)}{\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)}$$
for some $k≥2$ and $m≥n+k$?
references: [Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ n, ∃ m ≥ n + k, 25 = ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (m + i)) / ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i))

docstring:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?
references: [ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 1,
    Filter.limsup
        (fun n =>
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) *
            (↑(Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)))
        Filter.atTop =
      1

docstring: Is $n! + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => x.factorial + 1

docstring: Is $n! - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$?
type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos936.EventuallyNotPowerful fun x => x.factorial - 1

docstring: For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist?
references: [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
[Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal, Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ∃ a, {n | Erdos770.h n = ↑p}.HasDensity a

docstring:
If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is random, $|A| = \sqrt{p}$, can we almost surely cover
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $100\sqrt{p}$ translates of $A$? [Gr24]
references: [BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun p =>
      have k := (↑p).sqrt;
      have c := 100 * k;
      ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

docstring:
Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes
$2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most
$\frac{1}{10} N$?

We interpret "half the residue classes" as $\lfloor p_i / 2 \rfloor$.
references: [Er80] Erdős, Paul. "A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory." Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980): 89-115.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
    have remaining := {x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | ∀ (i : Fin 1000), ↑x ∉ A i};
    (∀ (i : Fin 1000), Nat.Prime (p i)) →
      StrictMono p → p 999 ^ 10 < N ^ 9 → (∀ (i : Fin 1000), (A i).card = p i / 2) → 10 * remaining.card ≤ N

docstring:
Suppose that a large sieve process leaves a set of quadratic size. Is that set quadratic?

The following very particular instance is probably the simplest [Gr24]:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ is a set with the property that
$|A \pmod p| \leqslant \frac{1}{2}(p + 1)$ for all sufficiently large $p$.
Is it true that either $|A \cap [X]| \ll X^{1/2} / \log^{100} X$, or $A$ is contained in the
image of $\mathbb{Z}$ under a quadratic map $\phi : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}$?
references: [GH14] Green, Ben, and Adam J. Harper. "Inverse questions for the large sieve." Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.4 (2014): 1167-1203.
[HV09] Helfgott, Harald Andrés, and Akshay Venkatesh. "How small must ill-distributed sets be." Analytic number theory 2 (2009): 224-234.
[Wa12] Walsh, Miguel N. "The inverse sieve problem in high dimensions." (2012): 2001-2022.
[Wa14] Walsh, Miguel N. "The algebraicity of ill-distributed sets." Geometric and Functional Analysis 24.3 (2014): 959-967.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    (∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Nat.Prime p → ((fun a => ↑a) '' A).ncard ≤ (p + 1) / 2) →
      ((fun X => ↑(A ∩ Set.Iic X).ncard) =O[Filter.atTop] fun X => √↑X / Real.log ↑X ^ 100) ∨
        ∃ P, P.degree = 2 ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, ∃ z, ↑a = Polynomial.eval (↑z) P

docstring:
Is there always a sum of two squares between $X - \frac{1}{10}X^{1/4}$ and $X$?
We formalize this as an eventual statement for sufficiently large real $X$.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ᶠ (X : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, Green66.IsSumOfTwoSquares n ∧ ↑n ∈ Set.Icc (X - 1 / 10 * X ^ (1 / 4)) X

docstring:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(b)** Are there infinitely many composite $n$ such that $f(n) > n^{1/2}$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] could not prove this. (Since $f(n) \ge p(n)$, the least prime factor of
$n$, there are infinitely many $n$ — those of the form $p^2$ — with $f(n) \ge n^{1/2}$; the
question asks for the strict inequality.) Here $f(n) > n^{1/2}$ is written as `(f n) ^ 2 > n`.
type_pretty: True ↔ {n | ¬Nat.Prime n ∧ 1 < n ∧ Erdos700.f n ^ 2 > n}.Infinite

docstring:
Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

This would have significant applications to Waring's problem. Erdős and Graham describe this as
'unattackable by the methods at our disposal'.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ ε > 0, (fun x => ↑x ^ (1 - ε)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Erdos323.f k k x)
